scope: phase_C_findings_recheck; supplied full current source/tests and explicitly labeled integration diff if present

findings.title: Cancellation acknowledged for still-running job is reported truthfully only by accident of shared state, but result of completed-after-cancel is delivered with no fence binding effect_lease in deliver_result's caller path
findings.issue: control('cancel') races with the worker: a cancel that lands while the job is leased invokes cancel_callback but the message still says 'Задача отменена.' even when the worker may still be running and later writes a result; more importantly, deliver_result only enforces effect_lease fencing when the caller passes one, so the durable_results path invoked from ingress never binds the currently leased effect job, allowing a cancelled/expired effect lease's result to be delivered.
findings.fix: Require an effect_lease (or equivalent durable effect job binding) for any delivery of an answer produced under an effect-mode lease, and reject delivery when the producing job was cancelled; make the cancel acknowledgement distinguish 'cancel requested' from 'cancelled'.

findings.title: Multi-part aggregate delivery can send remaining parts after a prior part already sent while aggregate stays unknown, contradicting no-blind-retry intent on partial failure
findings.issue: The aggregate is durably marked unknown before parts, and a part returning not 'sent' stops iteration, but an exception mid-loop (e.g. connection loss) leaves earlier parts possibly accepted; a later call returns the aggregate without resending, yet the loop's early return path for a non-'sent' part does not reconcile previously sent parts or mark the aggregate as such, so the reconciliation path for the aggregate has no per-part evidence.
findings.fix: Record per-part attempt rows and have reconciliation require provider evidence for every part before ever marking the aggregate sent; keep per-part outcomes in the aggregate payload.

findings.title: Notification codec/digest path trusts stored payload fields without strict schema validation of declared fields
findings.issue: deliver_watch pops source_scopes then passes the remainder to _notification_from_payload; the declared-fields contract depends entirely on that helper (not in packet) rejecting unknown/missing keys. The digest covers the full stored payload, but no local bounds on rendered text or title/summary lengths exist at delivery time.
findings.fix: Validate a strict allowlist of keys and per-field bounds in deliver_watch before reconstructing the notification, and cap rendered output length.

not_verified: prm/storage/jobs.py, policy.py, watch_jobs.py, actions.py, deletion.py, capabilities.py and bot/* are not in the packet; grant reservation/settlement semantics, _notification_from_payload strictness, and effect-lease creation are outside supplied source.
Runtime behavior against real PostgreSQL and the synthetic HTTP provider was not executed; conclusions are from static source review.
Whether deliver_result callers (bot/prm_handlers) pass effect_lease for effect-mode results cannot be verified here.
findings.summary: Recheck of the full current policy source resolves the review #37 P1 allegation against execute_reserved_groups: it revalidates grants under FOR UPDATE locks through the sender, and the new post-preparation revocation test plus _source_current (now applied to watch before sender) and durable source_scopes with legacy-origin recollection, source-before-subscription lock ordering, injected/DB clock wiring, and empty-media rejection all hold in the supplied source and tests. Remaining issues are a real P1 around delivery of results without a mandatory effect-lease/fence binding (ingress deliver_result path), plus two P2s on multi-part aggregate reconciliation evidence and notification payload bound checks. No P0; one P1 remains, so FIX_P1_FIRST.
